title: A Loop and a One-Way Trip

scenes.tts: This receptor brings L D L particles into the cell, where they are normally broken down. So how does the receptor hand its cargo to destruction, and escape, over and over?
scenes.narration: This receptor brings LDL particles into the cell, where they are normally broken down. So how does the receptor hand its cargo to destruction, and escape, over and over?
scenes.caption: This receptor brings LDL particles into the cell, where they are normally broken down. So how does the receptor hand its cargo to destruction, and escape, over and over?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD (fixed camera, kept for the whole film): a cross-section of one patch of cell edge filling the frame. A thick GREY plasma membrane runs across the top third. Above it, OUTSIDE, is a dark navy wash; below it, the CYTOSOL, a warm dark-grey wash. One large round EARLY ENDOSOME sits mid-frame, left of centre (about 30% of frame height); a smaller round LYSOSOME with a RED outline sits lower right. Rule for every lumen: the inside of every vesicle, endosome and lysosome is filled with the SAME navy wash as the outside. Colours by concept, whole film: receptor TEAL (a short bar crossing the membrane, with a stubby tail into the cytosol), LDL GOLD (a round particle), adaptors VIOLET (small blocks), clathrin GREY lattice of hexagons, dynamin ORANGE (a ring of beads), acid a ROSE tint. Slow ambient motion throughout: gold LDL particles drift in the outside wash; teal receptors jiggle slightly in the membrane. Build the world in the first 2 s, membrane first. Then: one teal receptor near top centre catches a drifting gold LDL (the LDL snaps onto its outer end). A fast schematic preview loop (about 4 s, tagged 'schematic' bottom right): a small bud carries the pair down into the endosome, the gold particle goes on into the red lysosome and shatters into small gold fragments, and the teal receptor glides back up to the membrane. On 'how does the receptor hand its cargo', two thin traces appear over the world: a TEAL closed loop through membrane and endosome, and a GOLD arrow from membrane to lysosome, each with a question mark. Text across the top, white, size 34: 'Cargo destroyed. Carrier saved. How?'

Title 'A Loop and a One-Way Trip' fades in over the top band for 2 s; the question text fades out under it. The two traces from the hook fade away. Gold LDL keeps drifting outside and receptors keep jiggling.

scenes.tts: L D L, in gold, carries cholesterol in the blood. Its receptor, in teal, spans the membrane and grips it from outside. Gripping, though, is not entering.
scenes.narration: LDL, in gold, carries cholesterol in the blood. Its receptor, in teal, spans the membrane and grips it from outside. Gripping, though, is not entering.
scenes.caption: LDL, in gold, carries cholesterol in the blood. Its receptor, in teal, spans the membrane and grips it from outside. Gripping, though, is not entering.
scenes.visual: Camera holds; the top-centre stretch of membrane brightens slightly. Three more gold LDL particles drift down and dock one by one on three teal receptors (each dock is a small snap with a gold flash). On 'grips it from outside', a white arrow label 'outside' points at the navy wash above, and 'cytosol' at the warm wash below (labels size 30). On 'not entering', the four bound pairs sit spread along the membrane; a faint white dashed arrow tries to point down through the membrane and fades out.

scenes.tts: The receptor's tail, inside the cell, must be gathered into a pit. Adaptors, in violet, do the gathering. They hold the receptor tails and the inner face of the membrane.
scenes.narration: The receptor's tail, inside the cell, must be gathered into a pit. Adaptors, in violet, do the gathering. They hold the receptor tails and the inner face of the membrane.
scenes.caption: The receptor's tail, inside the cell, must be gathered into a pit. Adaptors, in violet, do the gathering. They hold the receptor tails and the inner face of the membrane.
scenes.visual: Violet blocks rise from the cytosol and latch onto the teal tails under the membrane, one at a time, while also gripping the underside of the membrane (draw each violet block touching both a tail and the membrane line). As they latch, the four receptor-LDL pairs slide sideways along the membrane and cluster into one patch, top centre. Label 'adaptors' in violet, size 30, beside the first block.

scenes.tts: Then clathrin builds a cage of three-legged pieces beneath them. Clathrin holds neither membrane nor cargo; the adaptors do. As the cage grows, the membrane curves inward into a pit.
scenes.narration: Then clathrin builds a cage of three-legged pieces beneath them. Clathrin holds neither membrane nor cargo; the adaptors do. As the cage grows, the membrane curves inward into a pit.
scenes.caption: Then clathrin builds a cage of three-legged pieces beneath them. Clathrin holds neither membrane nor cargo; the adaptors do. As the cage grows, the membrane curves inward into a pit.
scenes.visual: Grey three-legged pieces (triskelion cartoons: a hub with three bent legs) fly in from the cytosol and lock together under the violet layer, building a grey hexagon-and-pentagon lattice. As the lattice grows, the membrane patch bends down into a deepening U-shaped pit with the receptors and gold LDL inside it. On 'holds neither membrane nor cargo', the grey lattice briefly dims and the violet blocks pulse to show they are the link. Label 'clathrin' in light grey, size 30, beside the lattice.

scenes.tts: Dynamin, in orange, wraps the narrow neck like a collar and, using energy from G T P, cuts it. The vesicle pinches free, and the cage falls away to be used again.
scenes.narration: Dynamin, in orange, wraps the narrow neck like a collar and, using energy from GTP, cuts it. The vesicle pinches free, and the cage falls away to be used again.
scenes.caption: Dynamin, in orange, wraps the narrow neck like a collar and, using energy from GTP, cuts it. The vesicle pinches free, and the cage falls away to be used again.
scenes.visual: The pit becomes a near-sphere joined to the membrane by a narrow neck. A ring of orange beads assembles around the neck and tightens (it visibly squeezes); the neck snaps, the membrane above reseals, and a free coated vesicle drifts down into the cytosol. The grey lattice then breaks into its three-legged pieces, which drift back up toward the membrane. The violet adaptors fall off too. Label 'dynamin' in orange, size 30, at the neck while it tightens.

scenes.tts: Look inside the vesicle. It still has the colour of the outside. The cargo is inside the cell, but no membrane has been crossed yet. Biologists say it is topologically outside.
scenes.narration: Look inside the vesicle. It still has the colour of the outside. The cargo is inside the cell, but no membrane has been crossed yet. Biologists say it is topologically outside.
scenes.caption: Look inside the vesicle. It still has the colour of the outside. The cargo is inside the cell, but no membrane has been crossed yet. Biologists say it is topologically outside.
scenes.visual: Slow push-in (scale 1.3x, centred on the vesicle) as the vesicle drifts toward the endosome. The vesicle's navy lumen pulses gently, and a thin white line links it to the navy outside wash above the membrane, which pulses in step. Label 'same as outside' in white, size 30, beside the lumen; on 'topologically outside' it morphs to 'topologically outside'. Push back out to the full world by the end of the scene.
Short rest while the vesicle drifts on toward the endosome (it keeps moving the whole time); the 'same as outside' label fades. Ambient drift continues.

scenes.tts: The vesicle fuses with an early endosome, the cell's sorting station. Receptor and L D L arrived together, still bound. If the receptor is to escape, they must part here. What is different about this compartment? Think about it.
scenes.narration: The vesicle fuses with an early endosome, the cell's sorting station. Receptor and LDL arrived together, still bound. If the receptor is to escape, they must part here. What is different about this compartment? Think about it.
scenes.caption: The vesicle fuses with an early endosome, the cell's sorting station. Receptor and LDL arrived together, still bound. If the receptor is to escape, they must part here. What is different about this compartment? Think about it.
scenes.visual: The vesicle touches the endosome; the two membranes merge into one bigger circle and the teal receptors, still holding gold LDL, now sit in the endosome membrane facing its lumen. Label 'early endosome' in white, size 30, above it. On 'they must part here', a small white bracket links each teal receptor to its gold particle. On 'What is different', the endosome brightens, the rest of the world dims to 50%, and a question card appears at the top, white, size 36: 'What is different about this compartment?'
Thinking pause: hold the question card. Only slow ambient motion: gold particles outside drift, the endosome outline breathes very slightly. Nothing is revealed.

scenes.tts: Its inside, the lumen, is mildly acid, kept that way by proton pumps. For L D L, at least, acid is the signal to let go of its receptor. This is the fork.
scenes.narration: Its inside, the lumen, is mildly acid, kept that way by proton pumps. For LDL, at least, acid is the signal to let go of its receptor. This is the fork.
scenes.caption: Its inside, the lumen, is mildly acid, kept that way by proton pumps. For LDL, at least, acid is the signal to let go of its receptor. This is the fork.
scenes.visual: The question card fades. A ROSE tint floods the endosome lumen from the rim inward (the world returns to full brightness). Small rose '+' dots enter through small pump blocks on the endosome membrane (labelled 'proton pumps', size 28). On-screen label in rose, size 30: 'mildly acid (pH about 6)'. On 'lets go', each gold LDL detaches and drifts into the middle of the lumen; each teal receptor's outer end folds back onto itself (a simple hinge fold, cartoon; small tag 'schematic'; not spoken). The white brackets from the earlier scene snap and fade.

scenes.tts: Here the paths split. Empty receptors slide into a thin tubule. It pinches off and carries them back to the surface, ready to grip again.
scenes.narration: Here the paths split. Empty receptors slide into a thin tubule. It pinches off and carries them back to the surface, ready to grip again.
scenes.caption: Here the paths split. Empty receptors slide into a thin tubule. It pinches off and carries them back to the surface, ready to grip again.
scenes.visual: A thin tubule grows out of the endosome's upper edge. The teal receptors slide into it; the gold LDL stays in the rose lumen. The tubule pinches off as a thin carrier and travels up to the plasma membrane, fuses, and the receptors unfold and stand upright in the membrane again. On 'ready to grip again', a drifting gold particle docks on one of them (small snap).

scenes.tts: The L D L stays behind. The endosome matures and passes it to a lysosome, the cell's digestion compartment. There, enzymes break it down and release its cholesterol.
scenes.narration: The LDL stays behind. The endosome matures and passes it to a lysosome, the cell's digestion compartment. There, enzymes break it down and release its cholesterol.
scenes.caption: The LDL stays behind. The endosome matures and passes it to a lysosome, the cell's digestion compartment. There, enzymes break it down and release its cholesterol.
scenes.visual: The endosome's label morphs from 'early endosome' to 'late endosome' (text morph, no Rab names). The endosome drifts toward the red lysosome at lower right and fuses with it; the gold LDL particles break into many small gold fragments, which spread out. Label in gold, size 30: 'cholesterol released'. The red-outlined compartment pulses once.
Rest beat. The world as it now stands: receptors back in the membrane, gold fragments in the lysosome. Ambient drift only; one new gold LDL docks on a receptor at the surface.

scenes.tts: So the receptor runs a loop: bind, enter, release, return. Its L D L makes a one-way trip to the lysosome. The two part at one place, the acid early endosome.
scenes.narration: So the receptor runs a loop: bind, enter, release, return. Its LDL makes a one-way trip to the lysosome. The two part at one place, the acid early endosome.
scenes.caption: So the receptor runs a loop: bind, enter, release, return. Its LDL makes a one-way trip to the lysosome. The two part at one place, the acid early endosome.
scenes.visual: Over the world, a TEAL line traces a closed loop through the four places the receptor visited (membrane patch, vesicle, endosome, tubule, back to membrane), with four teal labels appearing in order around it on each spoken word: 'bind', 'enter', 'release', 'return' (size 30). Then a GOLD line traces a one-way arrow from membrane through endosome to the lysosome. On 'part at one place', the endosome (rose) pulses and a white ring marks the fork where the teal and gold lines separate. Both lines stay on screen.
Rest beat: the teal loop and gold arrow stay on screen; a small teal dot runs once around the loop while a small gold dot runs the arrow and stops in the lysosome.

scenes.tts: In this simplest picture, binding and entry happen in order. Follow one batch of receptors, and a complete block of either stops its later handling. Release defects can reduce return rather than abolish it, so test each transition directly.
scenes.narration: In this simplest picture, binding and entry happen in order. Follow one batch of receptors, and a complete block of either stops its later handling. Release defects can reduce return rather than abolish it, so test each transition directly.
scenes.caption: In this simplest picture, binding and entry happen in order. Follow one batch of receptors, and a complete block of either stops its later handling. Release defects can reduce return rather than abolish it, so test each transition directly.
scenes.visual: The four teal labels light up in sequence like stations on a line, each lighting the next. Then, as a generic illustration with no named defect, the 'bind' label greys out and a grey bar labelled 'blocked' (size 30) drops across the loop at the membrane; the labels after it, 'enter', 'release', 'return', dim one after another, and the gold one-way arrow dims too. Small tag 'one batch, schematic' bottom right. Lift the bar and everything relights. Do NOT place the block between 'bind' and 'enter' or between 'release' and 'return' (the lesson's Predict boxes ask about those).

scenes.tts: That is how the carrier escapes: it lets go in acid, and leaves before the end. But in a patient's cells, which step has broken, and how could you tell?
scenes.narration: That is how the carrier escapes: it lets go in acid, and leaves before the end. But in a patient's cells, which step has broken, and how could you tell?
scenes.caption: That is how the carrier escapes: it lets go in acid, and leaves before the end. But in a patient's cells, which step has broken, and how could you tell?
scenes.visual: Camera holds on the full world with the two traces. A teal receptor at the surface catches a gold LDL and the loop pulses once around in teal while the gold particle runs the one-way arrow to the lysosome. On 'in a patient's cells', the traces fade back and three small grey dish icons slide in along the bottom edge, labelled 'patient cells' (size 28), each with a small white question mark.
End card over the dimmed world: 'The receptor runs a loop; its LDL makes a one-way trip.' in white, size 40, the word 'loop' in teal and 'one-way trip' in gold. Small 'biochemistrypedia.com' beneath.
